oneLiner: The world's largest construction and mining equipment maker, now also the AI buildout's power supplier through gensets and turbines. The market is betting that data-center power turns a cyclical into a multi-year annuity, and it is paying a multiple that needs the backlog to keep growing after 2027, not just convert.

verdict.stance: Cautious - priced for a power annuity
verdict.summary: Caterpillar is executing well: record margins, a backlog close to a year of sales, and orders out to 2029-2030. The problem is the bar. The reverse DCF needs free cash flow to grow ~16.6% a year for a decade against ~4.4% a year of revenue growth over the last three fiscal years, so the price assumes the power business re-rates the whole company. Our base case (FY2027 EPS ~$31 at 22x) is roughly flat to slightly below today, while the bear case (orders digest, EPS ~$23 at a cyclical 18x) loses over 40%, so the skew is negative. Two things would move us to Positive: Q3 backlog still rising with Power & Energy orders up, and a 2027 outlook that holds margins near 2026 levels despite tariffs.
wtb: Backlog keeps growing from the record $72B of Q2 2026: at or above ~$75B at Q3 (Oct 29, 2026) and not below $70B at Q4 2026.
FY2027 sales grow at least mid-single digits on a ~$78-79B FY2026 base (about $83B+), with power generation offsetting a softer construction year.
Net margin holds at ~16% or better in FY2027 (FY2027 EPS ~$30+) with net tariff cost no higher than the ~$2.2B of 2026.
The market keeps paying ~22x earnings at end-2027, which requires 2028 power orders to look flat-to-up rather than digesting.

bear.why: Hyperscaler 2027 capex digests and power orders are pushed out; backlog shrinks as it converts, construction weakens after the Q4 2026 dealer destock and tariffs stay a $2B+ cost. Sales slip to ~$77B, net margin falls to ~13.5% and the market goes back to a cyclical multiple on what now looks like peak-ish earnings.

base.why: The backlog converts steadily and the ~1.5GW capacity addition ships from Q4 2026; sales grow ~7% to ~$84B as power generation offsets flat construction. Net margin ~16.5% (in line with the 2026 run-rate) and buybacks shrink the count to ~450M. Power visibility earns a premium to the old mid-teens multiple, but not a growth multiple.

bull.why: Grid scarcity persists: turbine and large-engine slots sell out into 2030, backlog keeps setting records, mining re-equips on copper and U.S. infrastructure holds construction. Sales grow ~15% to ~$90B at a ~17.5% net margin, and the market prices Power & Energy as a structural growth franchise.

scenarioModel.note: FY2026 base assumes H1 actual $37.96B + Q3 consensus ~$20.3B + ~$20.2B Q4 = ~$78.5B (mid-to-high-teens growth on 2025's $67.6B). EPS = revenue x net margin / ~450M diluted shares (462.5M in Q2 2026, falling ~2% a year): bear $77B x 13.5% = $10.4B -> $23.1; base $84B x 16.5% = $13.9B -> $30.8; bull $90B x 17.5% = $15.75B -> $35.0. Multiples are applied to FY2027 EPS at end-2027. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Is the power backlog a multi-year annuity or the top of an order cycle?
debates.bull: Orders now reach 2029-2030 with price escalators, gas prime lead times run into late 2028-2029, and power generation sales to users rose 72% in Q2 2026; capacity, not demand, is the constraint.
debates.bear: The backlog nearly doubled in a year on one theme, Caterpillar does not disclose how much is data-center work, and only 59% ships within 12 months - pushouts and cancellations are how industrial backlogs unwind when capex digests.
debates.view: This is the debate that sets the multiple (18x vs 26x). We need to see orders keep running ahead of shipments after the capacity addition, not just a large number converting.

signpost.metric: Total backlog and Power & Energy order commentary
signpost.threshold: bullish if backlog at or above $75B with P&E orders up; bearish if backlog falls below $70B (book-to-bill under 1)

debates.q: Can margins hold near 2026 levels through tariffs, a dealer destock and a capacity ramp?
debates.bull: Price realization ($595M in Q2 2026) and volume more than absorbed tariffs; services are guided to grow faster than planned, and new capacity carries contracted pricing.
debates.bear: Excluding a $392M tariff-recovery benefit, management sees the 2026 adjusted margin near the bottom of its target range; Construction margins took a 340bp tariff hit in Q2 and a >$1B Q4 dealer destock is guided.
debates.view: The base case needs ~16.5% net margin in FY2027, roughly the 2026 run-rate. A guide that implies margin compression in 2027 would cut base EPS by ~$2 per point and move us toward the bear case.

signpost.metric: Adjusted operating margin and the first 2027 margin framework
signpost.threshold: below 20% adjusted operating margin in Q3, or a 2027 outlook implying lower margins, = bearish
signpost.when: Q3 report Oct 29, 2026; Q4 report and 2027 outlook, late Jan / early Feb 2027

debates.q: Does the price ask more than a cyclical can deliver?
debates.bull: Buybacks (diluted count -1.9% YoY) and cash conversion (TTM operating cash flow 125% of net income) mean per-share FCF can outgrow revenue; power is a higher-growth, services-heavy mix.
debates.bear: The reverse DCF needs FCF growth of ~16.6% a year for 10 years; revenue grew ~4.4% a year over the last three fiscal years, and every prior CAT up-cycle has ended with earnings and multiple falling together.
debates.view: The bar sits well above the track record, which is why we are Cautious rather than Neutral despite strong execution. The 2027 sales guide is the test: anything below mid-single-digit growth confirms the bar is too high.

signpost.metric: Initial FY2027 sales and revenue growth outlook
signpost.threshold: at least mid-single-digit growth = bar is reachable; flat or down = bear case
signpost.when: Q4 2026 report, late Jan / early Feb 2027

thesis: Power turned the steadiest segment into the growth engine. Data-center gensets and turbines drove power generation sales to users +72% and Power & Energy sales to users +33% in Q2 2026, with orders booked as far out as 2030.
Operating leverage is real, not just price. Adjusted operating margin expanded 430bp to 21.9% in Q2 2026 on $3.1B of volume, and management narrowed the 2026 tariff cost to the low end of its range.

Capacity is the moat in power. About 1.5GW of new large-engine and turbine capacity starts shipping in Q4 2026 and ramps over 18 months; rivals face the same lead times, and the dealer network turns the installed base into a services annuity.
Capital returns compound per share. ME&T free cash flow is guided to the top half of the $6-15B target range for 2026, funding buybacks that cut the diluted count ~1.9% a year.

latestProse: Q2 2026 (ended Jun 30; reported Aug 4). Sales and revenues of $20.54B rose 24% on $3.1B of volume and $595M of price, the first $20B quarter in company history. Adjusted EPS was $8.17 (GAAP $7.77) and adjusted operating margin expanded 430bp to 21.9%. All three primary segments grew double digits: Construction Industries +35% on North American infrastructure and rental fleet loading (dealer inventory built ~$400M), Resource Industries +20% on mining re-equipment, Power & Energy +17%. The disclosure that matters is the order book: backlog rose $9.4B in the quarter to a record $72.1B, nearly a full year of sales, with Power & Energy customers ordering out to 2029-2030. On the call management did not say how much of that backlog depends on data-center demand. Operating cash flow was $4.4B in the quarter, and $2.2B went to buybacks and dividends.
guidanceProse: FY2026 sales and revenue growth raised to the mid-to-high teens (from the April view), which implies roughly $78-80B against 2025's $67.6B. Net tariff cost narrowed to ~$2.2B, the low end of the prior $2.2-2.6B range; excluding $392M of tariff recoveries, the adjusted operating margin is expected near the bottom of the target range for that sales level. ME&T free cash flow is guided to the top half of the $6-15B annual range, capex holds at ~$3.5B for large-engine and turbine capacity, and services are expected to grow faster than previously planned. Flagged headwind: a more typical Construction Industries dealer inventory drawdown of over $1B in Q4. Q3 2026 consensus sits near $20.2-20.4B of revenue and ~$6.9 of adjusted EPS (Benzinga, Oct 2026).

guide.label: FY2026 sales growth guide
guide.sub: Raised Aug 4 | tariffs ~$2.2B | Q3 report Oct 29

segments: Power & Energy (~40% of Q2 2026 segment sales, ~$8.2B, +17%): reciprocating gensets, Solar Turbines, oil and gas, rail; the data-center growth engine, with ~1.5GW of added capacity shipping from Q4 2026.
Construction Industries (~41%, $8.35B, +35%): North American infrastructure and dealer rental fleets; most exposed to tariffs (340bp margin hit in Q2) and the guided >$1B Q4 destock.
Resource Industries (~23%, $4.65B, +20%): mining trucks and loaders, copper-led re-equipment; follows commodity prices.
Financial Products: dealer and customer financing, roughly $1B of quarterly revenue (unverified exact).
competitive: Cummins (CMI): the closest fight in data-center gensets; both are capacity-constrained on large engines.
Rolls-Royce (mtu), Wartsila, Generac and GE Vernova (large gas turbines): chase the same power backlog; none pairs it with CAT's dealer-and-services footprint across construction and mining.
Komatsu: the global number two in construction and mining equipment; competes on price and currency.
Deere (DE): ag-heavy mix in a softer 2026 cycle; the multiple gap to CAT is the market paying for power exposure.
moat: The dealer network is the moat: the largest independent dealer organization locks in parts, service and financing over a machine population measured in decades, turning services into an annuity on installed iron. In power, large-engine and turbine manufacturing scale plus a multi-year order book form a capacity moat rivals cannot quickly replicate.
risks: Order-cycle reversal. The backlog nearly doubled YoY on one theme; if 2027 hyperscaler capex digests, the conversion math runs in reverse through pushouts and cancellations, and CAT has not disclosed the data-center share.

Valuation bar above the track record. The price needs ~16.6% a year FCF growth for a decade against ~4.4% a year revenue growth over three years; in the bear case both EPS and the multiple compress, a loss of over 40%.
Tariffs and margin mix. Net tariff cost is ~$2.2B in 2026, the adjusted margin is near the bottom of the target range before recoveries, and policy remains volatile.
Capacity added into a possible peak. ~$3.5B of 2026 capex and an 18-month turbine and engine ramp create absorption risk if 2028 orders slow.
Construction and macro. The guided >$1B Q4 dealer destock tests retail demand; China construction stays weak and higher rates gate non-residential activity.
catalysts: Oct 28-30, 2026: MSFT, GOOGL, META, AMZN Q3 calls - 2027 capex guidance as the demand signal for the power backlog (debate 1).
Oct 29, 2026 (confirmed): Q3 2026 results - backlog, P&E orders and adjusted margin vs ~$20.3B / ~$6.9 consensus (debates 1, 2).
Q4 2026: first shipments from the ~1.5GW capacity addition; >$1B Construction dealer destock (debate 2).
Late Jan / early Feb 2027: Q4 2026 results and the first 2027 outlook (debates 2, 3).

valPresets.note: Base-year FCF is cyclically elevated (record margins, backlog conversion), so presets are deliberately modest and fade to a 2.5% terminal. Bear models a post-boom FCF decline, base a GDP-plus glide, bull a sustained power-scarcity ramp. Even the bull preset sits well below the ~16.6% a year the reverse DCF says is priced in.
